newsitem.title: INDIA: About 540,000 tonnes wheat arrive at Indian ports.
newsitem.headline: About 540,000 tonnes wheat arrive at Indian ports.

text.p: Nearly 540,000 tonnes of wheat imports had arrived at Indian ports up to last week, Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav said on Monday.
Yadav told parliament,"About 540,000 tonnes of imported wheat has arrived at Indian ports during this year up to March 4, 1997." He did not elaborate.
Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah told parliament on February 24 that India has so far contracted to import 1.68 million tonnes of wheat in fiscal 1996/97.
Ramaiah said in parliament that most of the wheat contracted was expected to arrive by the end of March.
He said some shipments from Canada might get delayed due to adverse weather there. He did not give details.
India expects a good wheat crop of about 64.5 million tonnes in 1996/97 (July/June), up from 62.6 million the previous season.
India produced 65.47 million tonnes of wheat in 1994/95. This year's crop is due for harvest in March after a ninth consecutive good monsoon.
In December, the federal government authorised the state-run State Trading Corporation (STC) to import up to two million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 to augment supplies and check domestic prices.
